Yes—this public, computational Perturb-seq benchmark is answerable in principle.

**High-level analysis:** Additive baseline modeling of single-perturbation pseudobulk deltas (summing the two constituent single-gene control-relative profiles per double condition), followed by residual analysis against that baseline to assign interaction classes (additive when the observed matches the sum; synergy/suppression when the joint response is amplified/dampened; neomorphic when the residual points in a direction absent from either single). Confidence would come from replicate consistency and single-perturbation signal strength; falsifiers would be stated as the residual pattern (magnitude/direction on specified F-features) that, if observed at private scoring, would contradict the assigned class.

Per the probe instruction, no predictions calculated here.
